title: Fox Signs YouTube Stars to Make Cool New Shows — And Lets Them Do Whatever They Want!
summary: Imagine you have a YouTube channel with millions of fans. Now imagine a big TV company comes to you and says, “We’ll pay for your next show, and you can make it exactly how you want!” That’s what’s happening with Fox Creator Studios. They just signed deals with seven super-popular online creators. One is Josh Richards, a Canadian influencer with a sketch comedy show. Another is Emelia Hartford, a racing star who’s starting a celebrity interview series on race tracks called “Hot Laps.” There are also food creators, a group called Speeed Co, and more. Together, these creators have 65 million followers! Usually, when a big company pays for a show, they get to make lots of changes and give notes. But Fox is doing something unusual. Billy Parks, the head of Fox Creator Studios, said, “We don’t give notes.” That means the creators have full creative control. Fox just helps with money and selling ads. Parks says he’s looking for “different types of creators who are trying different things.” He’s even open to creators who use AI tools to make content. “If it’s a good story, well told, we’re here,” he said. This is a big deal because it shows that big media companies are finally trusting online creators to know what their audiences want. And for us viewers, it means we might get way more fun, weird, and original shows made by the people we already love to watch.
why_it_matters: This is a sign that the way we watch shows is changing — kids and teens have more influence than ever on what gets made, and their favorite internet stars might soon be on regular TV too.

keywords.explanation: Fox Creator Studios is a part of the Fox TV company that works directly with online video makers.
An influencer is a person who has many followers on social media and can affect what those fans like or buy.
Sketch comedy is a series of short, funny scenes or skits, usually with different characters and jokes.
A celebrity interview series is a set of talk shows where famous people are asked questions in a fun setting.
Creative control means the power to decide how a show is made, without someone else changing your ideas.
AI tools are computer programs that can create pictures, videos, or text by learning from data.

background_read: YouTube stars like Josh Richards (a Canadian influencer) and Emelia Hartford (a female racing star) have huge online audiences that TV companies want to reach.
Fox is a major television network that usually controls the look and script of its shows, so giving all power to creators is a new experiment.
Many young viewers now watch more YouTube and TikTok than regular TV, so big media companies are changing how they make entertainment to stay popular.
Article_Structure: WHO: Fox Creator Studios and seven popular online creators, like Josh Richards and Emelia Hartford
WHAT: Signed deals giving the creators full control to make new shows while Fox pays and sells ads
WHERE: The shows will likely appear on TV and online platforms
WHY: Because Fox believes that creators know what their fans want and that unique, original content will bring in viewers

perspectives.description: They are thrilled because they can make whatever they dream up without a company changing their vision, and they get paid to do it.
They think this is a smart way to attract younger audiences and find the next big hit, even if it means taking a risk on untraditional ideas.
Some people worry that without guidance, the shows might be poorly made or that Fox is just trying to cash in on famous names.
